subject: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking & target $/1M tokens (Re: Redwood vs hosts)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking & target $/1M tokens

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a targeted pricing recommendation: 

Summary from our call:
- Expected steady-state requests: ~45M tokens/month (inference tokens) with spikes to ~120M in peak months.
- Primary workload: chat-style LLM (context lengths 2k-4k), occasional embedding batch jobs (~10M embeddings/month).
- Hard constraint: procurement needs a target unit cost to model TCO for FY27.

As discussed, could you confirm two things so we can finalize the economics: 
1) Target range for $/1M tokens that would make a Redwood proposal viable for Acme (e.g., $8-12 / 1M tokens), and
2) Any minimum commitment window you need (monthly vs annual) and whether you can consider a committed spend in exchange for lower unit pricing.

I attached a short benchmark deck and a pricing spreadsheet that outline typical Redwood unit economics vs other hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic), including how batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles affect the effective $/1M tokens.

Next steps: if you confirm the target $/1M and commitment window, I’ll pull together 3 options (on-demand, 12mo commit, 24mo commit) with expected net effective $/1M and operational SLAs.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: token_benchmark_deck.pdf, redwood_token_model_pricing.xlsx

From: Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking & target $/1M tokens

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the materials. Quick answers: 

1) Target $/1M tokens: ideally we need to be at or below $12 / 1M tokens for the steady-state chat workload to make this competitive vs our internal hosting options. If you can get to ~$8 / 1M at scale with a commitment, that would make a strong case.
2) Commitment: procurement prefers 12-month committed spend but we can consider 24-month if pricing is significantly better. For initial negotiations they'd likely ask for an annual committed spend tied to SLAs.

One more data point: our CFO asked for the net effective price after savings from caching/batching — so if you can show an example that maps list $/1M to an \"effective\" $/1M after typical platform optimizations, that will help.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Williams
Head of AI Platform, Acme Corp
sam.williams@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: Pricing examples + effective $/1M after optimizations

Sam — good notes, thanks. Below is an initial illustrative mapping (I'll attach the spreadsheet tab with the worked example):

Illustrative unit economics (chat workload, 2-4k context):
- Redwood list price (on-demand): $14 / 1M tokens
- Redwood effective price with batching + KV caching + quantization profile: $7-9 / 1M tokens (assuming 20-40% token reduction from caching and 25-40% CPU/GPU efficiency uplift from batching/quantization)
- OpenAI (public API comparable model): ~$20-22 / 1M tokens (list public pricing for comparable models; effective savings limited unless using your own caching layer)
- Anthropic (public API): ~$18-20 / 1M tokens
- Self-hosted on open-model hosts (infra-only providers): list rates widely vary - raw infra cost could be ~$5-15 / 1M tokens but does not include platform engineering, ops, and SLAs (so TCO often higher for teams without production ops).

Key assumptions: cache-hit rates ~10-30% for chat prefix caching; batching efficiency depends on latency SLO - we modeled a conservative 25% batching gain for this example. The attached spreadsheet has sensitivity rows so you can see effective $/1M across hit-rate and batching ranges.

Attachments included in this message: redwood_token_model_pricing.xlsx (tab: \"Acme worked example\"), token_benchmark_deck.pdf (summary slides).

If Acme's procurement is comfortable with a 12mo commitment, our standard committed tier would push the list to $10 / 1M and effective to ~$6-7 / 1M at your stated volumes (45M steady-state; 120M peak). For 24mo/greater commit we can structure additional volume tiers that approach $5-6 / 1M effective.

If this looks directionally right, I’ll work with Marissa and Aditya to draft 3 formal options (A/B/C) with SLAs, commit levels, and an example SOW for embedding batch jobs.

Best — Vanessa

Marissa/Aditya — forwarding Sam's reply and my worked example. Ask: can you draft three external-facing pricing options we can present to Acme by EOD tomorrow?

Quick requirements: 
- Option A (On-demand): list unit price and minimal commitment; show effective $/1M at Acme steady-state volumes.
- Option B (12mo commit): price at commit that targets list ~$10 / 1M and effective ~$6-7 / 1M, include standard SLA language.
- Option C (24mo or higher commit): deeper volume tiers that can approach $5 / 1M effective; include sample SOW for embedding batch jobs and a discount table.

Also include a short bullets section for procurement: billing cadence, termination notice, audit logs/KMS options (Sam flagged compliance as important). I’ve attached the same spreadsheet and deck for numbers.

Thanks — Vanessa
